resolutions.researcher_notes: Offshore Technology's Wafa-Mellitah pipeline market-data page states the corridor is 'Operational since 2004.' Mellitah Oil & Gas's own gas-division production page describes the Wafa field gathering stations and Wafa-to-Mellitah pipeline system in current-tense, ongoing-operations terms, consistent with 'operating.' No source found suggesting a shutdown or suspension of this corridor. NOTE (see __REDUNDANCY__ below): both sources describe the 525km onshore corridor as TWO PARALLEL lines (32in gas + 16in oil/condensate); status support here applies to the corridor generally, not specifically to a 16in *gas* service, since independent sources consistently attribute the 16in line to oil/condensate, not gas.

Offshore Technology gives the Wafa-Mellitah corridor as '525 kilometers' (stated for both the 32in gas and 16in oil pipeline market-data entries, which it treats as parallel lines of the same length). Mellitah Oil & Gas's Company Achievements page states: 'The 525 Km onshore pipeline system comprises of 32" gas and 16" oil/condensates pipelines' running from Wafa Desert Plant to Mellitah. GEM's value (524.65 km) is consistent with these (rounds to ~525 km); no contradiction, just rounding precision. Both sources describe this as the combined/shared corridor length for BOTH parallel lines, not a length unique to a 16in gas service.

Mellitah Oil & Gas's own Wafa Field site page confirms the field (NC169A concession, ~540 km SW of Tripoli, ~160 km south of Ghadames, on the Libya-Algeria border) has a 'Gas compression station to Mellitah' and a separate 'Oil pumping station to Mellitah' -- i.e. two distinct pipeline take-off points at Wafa field itself, one per commodity. Offshore Technology's Wafa-Mellitah Gas pipeline page corroborates Wafa as the originating field (pipeline named for it; start point given as Wadi Al-Shatii, the district housing the field infrastructure). FuelSource='Wafa Gas Field' is well supported for the corridor generally. Flag: the Wafa-field page's explicit split into a separate gas compression station vs. oil pumping station is itself independent, primary-source evidence for the redundancy question below.

Mapcarta's map entry titles the field 'Al-Wafa Oil Field - Mellitah & Eni Oil and Gas Company Map - Nalut, Libya', supporting StartLocation=Wafa Gas Field / StartPrefecture=Nalut. Offshore Technology's Wafa-Mellitah Gas pipeline page gives explicit endpoints 'Wadi Al-Shatii' (start) to 'Nuqat Al-Khams' (end), directly matching GEM's EndPrefecture/District='Nuqat al Khams district'. Mellitah Oil & Gas's own Mellitah Complex page (not cited here as a primary ref for this cell, see other units) further situates the complex '~22km east of Zwara City', which sits within Nuqat al Khams district, corroborating the endpoint. One inconsistency to flag: Offshore Technology's separate Wafa-Mellitah OIL pipeline entry lists its end point as 'Zawiya' rather than 'Nuqat Al-Khams' -- this likely reflects downstream product movement from the Mellitah complex onward toward the Zawiya refinery (a separate onward pipeline/product stream), since Mellitah Oil & Gas's own Mellitah-Complex page states Wafa oil/condensate is processed and blended AT Mellitah (Wafa Coastal Plant, part of the Mellitah Complex) and the Mellitah blend is 'exported from Mellitah terminal' -- not that the 16in Wafa pipeline itself bypasses Mellitah to terminate at Zawiya. Treated as a minor inconsistency on Offshore Technology's auto-generated market-data page, not a contradiction of GEM's EndLocation.

STRONG, CORROBORATED FINDING: P6705 (16in) is misclassified -- the 16in Wafa-Mellitah line is the OIL/CONDENSATE line, not a gas line, and does not belong in the gas tracker. Every source found that distinguishes the two parallel Wafa-Mellitah lines by diameter+service agrees, with no exceptions: (1) Offshore Technology's 'Wafa-Mellitah Gas' market-data page: 32in max diameter, carries natural gas / 'on-specification gas', ~13 MMSm3/day. (2) Offshore Technology's separate 'Wafa-Mellitah Oil' market-data page: 16in max diameter, product type 'Crude oil' (condensate). (3) Mellitah Oil & Gas Company Achievements page (operator's own site): 'The 525 Km onshore pipeline system comprises of 32" gas and 16" oil/condensates pipelines. Both pipelines run in parallel from Wafa Desert Plant to Mellitah... the sale gas is exported to Italy and the oil/condensate, after further treatment for LPG fractionation, is exported.' (4) Mellitah Oil & Gas gas-division production page: '32 inches... Carries: On-specification sales gas... ~13 MMSm3/day' vs '16 inches... Carries: Oil and condensate mixture... ~23,000 bbl/d NGL and ~38,000 bbl/d oil/condensate.' (5) Mellitah Oil & Gas Wafa-field site page: the field has a separate 'Gas compression station to Mellitah' and 'Oil pumping station to Mellitah' -- two distinct facilities/lines at the source. (6) Mellitah Oil & Gas Mellitah-Complex page: the Wafa Coastal Plant (within Mellitah Complex) specifically processes 'oil and natural gas liquids from the Wafa field', separately from the Mellitah Plant which handles gas/condensate from the offshore Sabratha platform (Bahr Essalam field) -- i.e. the Wafa-sourced onshore stream landing via the 16in line is treated as an oil/NGL stream, not sales gas. No source anywhere describes a 16in GAS line on this corridor, or a 32in oil/condensate line. CONCLUSION: P6705 (16in, currently in GGIT/gas tracker as 'Wafa-Mellitah Gas Pipeline') and P0484 (32in) are NOT duplicate/redundant entries of the same pipeline -- they are two real, physically distinct, genuinely parallel pipelines, correctly kept as separate rows. But P6705 is in the WRONG TRACKER: by diameter and service it is the oil/condensate line and belongs in GOIT (oil tracker), not GGIT. ACTION FLAG: gem.wiki already has a page titled 'Wafa-Mellitah_Oil_Pipeline' (surfaced incidentally in web search results during this research), which suggests GEM/GOIT may already carry this pipeline as a separate oil-tracker entry under that name -- before reclassifying/moving P6705, check GOIT for an existing 'Wafa-Mellitah Oil Pipeline' row to avoid creating a duplicate; if one already exists, P6705's gas-tracker row is likely a redundant/erroneous entry that should be removed (or corrected in place) rather than moved.
